title: From Madagascar to Accra: Reflections from the Language Diversity Conference 2026
content:
Participating in the Language Diversity Conference 2026 in Accra, Ghana, was a meaningful experience for me, both personally and as someone working to strengthen the presence of the Malagasy language in the digital world.

The conference brought together more than 100 language activists, Wikimedians, researchers, and heritage workers representing 82 languages. For three days, Accra became a space for sharing experiences, learning from different communities, and discussing how languages can remain visible and active in an increasingly digital world.

The conference opened with Jara dance, Nbangba Cultural Troupe from Ghana, immediately bringing a strong sense of culture, identity, and community into the event. It was a beautiful way to begin a conference about languages. Before the keynote, presentations, and discussions even started, we were already seeing that language is closely connected to culture, traditions, identity, and the way communities express themselves.

That cultural atmosphere remained present throughout the conference.

I was particularly happy to see the Malagasy language represented at an international conference dedicated to language diversity.

title: Inaugural Wikimedia Kimaragang Online Meetup: Strengthening Community, Empowering Digital Knowledge
content:
Following the previous physical meetup, the Wikimedia Kimaragang Community successfully organized its Online Meetup Series 1 on September 19, 2026, from 8:00 PM to 9:00 PM. This first online gathering for the community was conducted under the guidance of the Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia (WCUGM). The session, moderated by the meetup coordinator (Blusjai), was attended by 10 Kimaragang community members, 2 WCUGM representatives (Tofeiku, Rulwarih), and 1 representative from the Kadazandusun Language community (Jjurieee).

The session began with an introduction to the Wikimedia Foundation and WCUGM. During this briefing, emphasis was placed on Wikimedia’s core mission: making knowledge freely accessible to all. This mission was directly linked to the potential of the Kimaragang ethnic group to enhance global access to information regarding their culture and language. Additionally, Wikimedia platforms were highlighted as a space for the community to interact and exchange ideas without geographical boundaries.

title: Wiki for Human Rights Nigeria: First Language Wikipedia Physical Training
content:
In August, Wiki for Human Rights Nigeria launched its first-language Wikipedia physical training. Since the start of the project catering to LGBTIQ+ people, the organization has mostly focused on training queer people to edit Wikipedia, add structured data on Wikidata, upload images to Wikimedia Commons, and become acquainted with what Wikimedia projects entail. Still, we never explored what it means to contribute to the local-language Wikimedia projects.

Much of the early work on queer topics on Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba Wikipedia came through our writing contests. Those contributions matter, but our goal now is to grow a community of editors who stay with this work beyond a contest, as allies invested in advancing queer rights in Nigeria. This organizing has also come at a cost: I have received hostile messages from people opposed to our work, which is part of why building a committed, supportive community matters so much.

title: Wikimedians from Central and Eastern Europe go beyond the crossroads in Cluj-Napoca
content: This year’s Wikimedia CEE Meeting took place in Cluj-Napoca from 18–20 September under the slogan “Beyond the Crossroads”. A total of around 140 participants representing about 35 communities and affiliates, including delegates from closely associated communities outside of the region of Central and Eastern Europe, had the opportunity to share knowledge and exchange ideas. The conference was held at the Babeș-Bolyai University.

title: Navigating Challenging Spaces – supporting volunteers in the movement
content:
As we reflect on the global trends affecting the movement, community health and community support, both for existing editors and newcomers, are thrown into sharp relief, as is the role that those supporting those communities – affiliate staff and volunteers in particular – can play in supporting that community. 

“Working towards a toolkit” – Navigating Challenging Topics

In January 2026, Wikimedia UK, in partnership with the Volunteer Supporters Network Hub pilot and Wikimedia LGBT+, held the event Navigating challenging topics: Creating a toolkit for supporting editors, featuring speakers and discussion to bring together best practice for supporting editors working in more challenging areas on-wiki.

title: WikiRempah Photowalk in Palembang, Knowledge of Traditional Textiles from the Land of Sriwijaya
content:
While WikiRempah’s previous efforts focused on documenting historical sites, local cuisine, or traditional practices, this time the initiative has expanded to include a photowalk to highlight traditional textiles.

This initiative involved the Palembang Wikimedia Community visiting Kriya Sriwijaya to document various types of textiles, ranging from batik, jumputan, gambo, and songket.

The participation of Msdlfsalsa, Chaejhh, Librarean, and Who’sisthis wirh Nasywaaf as coordinator, marked a significant milestone in spreading knowledge about traditional textiles from Palembang. Meanwhile, the online team consisted of Ana Ainina, Supardi Sahabu, and Sofi Solihah, who hail from Java, Gorontalo, and Manado, respectively.

It is important to note that the songket weaving tradition in Palembang is often linked to the era of the Sriwijaya Kingdom, which flourished from the 7th to the 13th centuries. According to Palembang folk tales passed down through generations, the tradition of songket weaving began with an encounter between Chinese merchants carrying silk and Indian and Middle Eastern merchants carrying gold.

title: Celebrating Big Butterfly Month with a Day of Butterflies, Learning and Creativity
content:
September was celebrated as Big Butterfly Month, a whole month dedicated to these beautiful winged jewels. During the month, butterfly walks, learning sessions, awareness programmes and other activities were organised to bring people closer to butterflies and nature.

As part of the celebration, a full-day butterfly exhibition, workshop and drawing competition was organised in collaboration with Wiki Loves Butterfly (WLB), The Puppeteers, a puppetry and art group based in Bardhaman and Big Butterfly Month. Around 40 students from different schools in Bardhaman took part in the programme.

The programme was designed as a fun and interactive experience where children could observe, learn and connect with nature through butterflies and art.

title: Videos documenting banking terms produced in Macedonian Sign Language
content:
Following the successful implementation of a project aimed at producing videos documenting economic and legal terms in the Macedonian Sign Language during the first half of 2024, Wikimedia MKD renewed the collaboration with the economic experts and a professional interpreter in the production of videos documenting banking terms. These activities were carried out from February to August 2026 and resulted in a total of 40 videos produced. The project was supported by external funding from a grant extended by a Macedonian commercial bank.

The main change is that this project was fully funded from external sources. Unlike the inaugural project, which was financially supported by the Wikimedia Foundation, this one was carried out with funding from a commercial bank through a call for grant applications to support and promote projects pertaining to social inclusion of people with disabilities in the Macedonian society.

title: My WikiGap 2026 Journey in Uganda: Amplifying women’s stories through Wikimedia
content:
I had the privilege of being part of the organising team for WikiGap 2026 in Uganda, an initiative led by the Wikimedia Community User Group Uganda. I served as the Communications Lead (COT), supporting the campaign’s communication, visibility, and engagement efforts.

WikiGap 2026 in Uganda was led by Zahara Nabagala and Emmanuel Oruk, who served as the Project Leads, with support from Community Manager Will Ssemanda and Executive Director Michael Kaluba. Their leadership, coordination, and support were instrumental in guiding the campaign from planning through implementation and in bringing together organisers, mentors, and participants around the shared   goal of improving the representation of women on Wikimedia platforms.

WikiGap 2026 was more than just an editing campaign for me. It was an opportunity to contribute to a global movement that seeks to address the gender gap in Wikimedia projects by ensuring that the stories, achievements, and contributions of women are better represented in the world’s largest free knowledge platforms.

title: My Road to Wiki journey: from Cohort 2 to meeting the community in person
content:
From a curious student to a contributor, and the day we finally met in person

I’ve been part of the Wikimedia movement for a little over a year, and on 2 October 2026 the Road to Wiki Cohort 2 came to a close. We met our mentors and the community in person, and I realised how much more this program had given me than I expected when I joined. This is my attempt to write down what I did, who helped me, and what it left me with.

  • I came in through WikiClub Tech, part of Open Knowledge Initiatives (OKI). It’s a student led platform meant to bridge academia and industry, so students get practical experience by contributing to Wikimedia through technology.
  • My learning path was Road to Wiki Cohort 2026. The program deliberately reaches Tier 2 and Tier 3 engineering colleges in India, and my own college, United University, is one of them. Its Wikimania 2026 proposal says Cohort 2 expanded to 8 colleges and 250+ new students.
  • The reason it exists is a gap I lived myself. India has plenty of technical talent, but very few visible pathways from a classroom into a large open-source project like MediaWiki. Nobody had told us this was possible, and Road to Wiki did.

title: Wikimedia Spain is holding its Annual Conference in Zamora to highlight the value of local knowledge
content:
This weekend, Zamora served as a meeting point to discuss free knowledge, heritage and open culture. The 12th Annual Wikimedia Spain Conference brought together, over three days at the Ethnographic Museum of Castile and León (MECyL), volunteers from the Wikimedia community, professionals from the fields of culture and heritage, teachers, researchers, institutions and members of the public with an interest in open culture. 

The event was attended by around fifty people, who over the course of these three days were able to share their experiences, knowledge and reflections on free knowledge and open culture. 

Under the slogan “Free knowledge is built from the territory”, the conference focused on the role of communities and local areas in building knowledge that is accessible to everyone. 

A significant proportion of the knowledge generated in cities and regions has yet to be documented, verified and shared online. Heritage, traditions, local histories, people and institutions are all sources of knowledge that can help to expand and improve the content available on projects such as Wikipedia.

title: A Journey to the Language Diversity Conference 2026 in Accra, Ghana
content:
Languages are more than tools for communication. They carry memory, humour, belief and identity from one generation to the next. For those of us who belong to communities whose languages are barely visible online, the question of how to keep them alive in the digital age is not abstract; it is personal and urgent. It was with this question in mind that I travelled to Accra, Ghana, for the Language Diversity Conference 2026, held from 2 to 4 October.

The conference was themed “Strengthening Language Communities in the Open Knowledge Movement.” It is a global gathering dedicated to advancing linguistic diversity within the Wikimedia community and the wider open movement. Bringing together editors, researchers, language advocates and institutional partners, it offered a rare space for communities working on under-resourced languages to learn from one another and to be heard. I was fortunate to attend as a scholarship recipient of the Wikimedia Foundation, after a highly competitive application process that opened in early 2026. This essay is my account of the journey, the sessions that shaped me, and what I carry back to my own community.

title: AI and the Future of Wikimedia: Reflections from WCNA 2026
content: During a wrap-up session for WikiConference North America 2026, a participant commented that they were glad the conference program hadn’t focused too heavily on AI. While I agree, I also couldn’t help noticing a sense of unease among participants about the rapid developments in generative AI over the past five years and what they mean for the Wikimedia movement. There is broad agreement that AI is here to stay, but there is little clarity about its implications for the projects and the future of Wikimedia. At the same time, I learned a lot about how the movement is adapting to these developments. In this piece, I reflect on what I learned in the AI and Tech track sessions and in conversations with conference participants. I decided to write down my thoughts primarily to help me wrap my head around this complex topic, but I hope it might also help some readers find answers to their questions and get involved in the conversation.
